title: Using Ratibida pinnata, Monarda fistulosa, and Echinacea purpurea to determine the Effects of Cold Stratification, Plant-derived Smoke and Ash, and Rinsing on the Germination and Growth of Prairie Species
why: Web search 'Ratibida columnifera OR Ratibida pinnata germination gibberellic acid OR potassium nitrate OR smoke OR dormancy'. title: Effects of Different Practices on Seed Germination of Some Weeds Which is used as Medical
why: Web search 'Senecio vulgaris OR Senecio inaequidens seed germination gibberellic acid OR potassium nitrate OR smoke'. The abstract (Kahramanmaras Sutcu Imam Univ J Nat Sci 18(4): 48-54, 2015) says S. vulgaris germinated best under a 16 h light / 8 h dark cycle and at 15 C, a light-duration trial that would close sense_light_nonvisual for S. vulgaris. The abstract was read through a fetch tool that returned fragments only, so no whole-sentence quote could be checked; the full text is unread. No DOI on the page.

authors: Michael W. Olszewski, Grant J. Folin
title: Germination Responses of Purpletop and Big Bluestem Caryopses Subjected to Prechilling, Sodium Hypochlorite, and Storage
why: Web search 'Andropogon gerardii OR big bluestem seed germination smoke OR gibberellic acid OR potassium nitrate OR karrikinolide'. HortScience 44(5): 1407-1411 (2009), found on the wildflower.org literature record id 1027, which lists no DOI. It compares prechilling in water or potassium nitrate, a sodium hypochlorite soak and storage on Andropogon gerardii. The ASHS abstract says prechilling improved big bluestem only in distilled water and that NaOCl had little or no effect on it; the KNO3 result for big bluestem is not stated whole, so the trial is a lead for sense_chemical and the full text is unread.
queries: web: Andropogon gerardii OR "big bluestem" seed germination smoke OR gibberellic acid OR potassium nitrate OR karrikinolide

title: The role of insect visitors of Glechoma hederacea (Lamiaceae) and Anthriscus sylvestris (Umbelliferae) as pollinators
why: Web search 'Glechoma hederacea pollination biology flower longevity nectar anthesis floral biology'. A University of Groningen master's thesis (2002); its abstract says G. hederacea produces nectar faster during the day than at night, a day-night floral measurement that may state flower opening or nectar timing in hours. Nectar rate is not flower opening or scent timing by itself, so the diel cell stays open until the thesis is read.
